topics.label: Course and lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the administrative welcome and introduces the learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain conventional cancer treatment approaches that physically remove or non-specifically damage dividing cells, alongside their systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on selectively eliminating cancer cells by exploiting their intrinsic vulnerabilities, such as hormonal dependencies, checkpoint deficiencies, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and overcoming resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how small-molecule inhibitors target hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and address the subsequent emergence of drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on engineered monoclonal antibodies used as targeted therapeutics, both as direct receptor inhibitors and as delivery vehicles for cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological principles and clinical approaches involved in mobilizing and engineering the adaptive immune system against cancer.

topics.label: Clinical progress, challenges, and future perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overarching assessment of clinical progress in cancer therapy while considering persistent challenges, future innovations, and ethical dilemmas.
